notes:
Account snapshot: large fintech with real-time personalization and chat support workflows. Primary ask = Dedicated capacity with strict latency SLOs + predictable throughput under market open hours spikes.

Key SLO alignment (what client cares about):
- Wants p50/p95/p99 definitions for both streaming and non-streaming paths; specifically: p95 non-streaming (end-to-end, client-to-client) target ~120-200ms for short prompts; p95 streaming first-byte target ~100-150ms, and sustained token throughput p95 per-token <20ms on server-side (they measure both first-byte and per-token).
- Client emphasized: "We need user perceived latency guarantees — what matters is finger-to-response, not just server CPU time." They will provide synthetic UX traces.
- Ask to clearly separate measurement planes: client-side (full RTT from user device), edge/proxy time, Redwood server processing (inference compute), and downstream post-processing. Agreement needed on which plane SLOs are contractually enforced vs advisory.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: they run both. For streaming chat they want deterministic first-token behavior + steady per-token pacing. For non-streaming batch/generation (single-request completions) they want tighter p95 on completion latency.
- Percentiles: prefer p50/p95/p99 for reporting; will require daily histograms and rolling 30d trend for regressions. Requests for percentile measurement method: rank-based at 1s granularity with outlier trimming during deploy events.

Capacity & throughput expectations:
- Peak window: 1800 RPS for short-chat requests with typical 40 token responses; sustained background embedding jobs ~200 RPS (batched).
- Target steady-state tokens/sec: ~45k tokens/sec aggregate during peak (after batching).
- Desired headroom: 2x buffer over predicted peak for autoscaling and guaranteed throughput. They want reserved GPU planning for steady baseline + burst pool.
- Model preferences: 70% runs on an LLaMA-derivative 13B quantized for cost, 30% on a higher-quality 33B model during peak for privileged flows. Need Redwood to qualify quantized variant performance.

SLA negotiation points called out by legal/ops:
- Availability SLA: 99.95% (monthly) + credit schedule.
- Latency SLOs: contractually enforceable for server-side processing time (p95), advisory for client-to-client latency unless Redwood runs edge proxy. Client to propose acceptable mapping table.
- Measurement & dispute process: daily SLO dashboard + 30d telemetry export; 15-day dispute window; Redwood to provide raw traces for missed-window investigations.

Measurement & instrumentation recommendations we proposed: 
- Two-tier metrics: server-side inference timing (first-byte, per-token) instrumented at runtime (rt.round_trip, rt.first_byte, rt.per_token_avg) and e2e synthetic probes executed from client regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
- Define canonical synthetic workload: replay 10k user traces extracted from production anonymized logs, plus uniform token-length buckets (0-32, 33-128, 129-512).
- Warm-up policy: exclude first 5 minutes after rolling deploys for contractual p95 calculations; capture deploy annotations in telemetry.
- Batching/KV cache impacts: capture request-level batching size and cache hit tags so latency percentiles can be sliced by batching, cache-hit, model-variant.

POC proposal (agreed on call):
- 2-week Dedicated POC in eu-west and us-east: reserve baseline (equivalent of 8 x A100-80GB capacity) + 2x burst pool non-reserved GPUs. Objective: validate p95 non-streaming <=150ms (server-side) and streaming first-byte p95 <=120ms under 75% of predicted peak.
- Deliverables: SLO dashboard access, daily telemetry export, model perf profile, cost per 1M tokens calculation, and a proposed SLA redline with latency credit matrix.

Open questions / negotiation items:
- How to map client-measured (finger-to-response) to server-side SLOs for consumer-facing contracts? They want clear guidance and a conversion rubric.
- Exact penalty thresholds for p99 regressions — legal prefers caps.
- Need commitment on on-call escalation + runbook for incident classification (latency degradation vs availability).

Stated quotes from CTO: "If we can get predictable p95s during market hours, we will convert — but it has to be deterministic, not 'best-effort'."

Sales notes (shorthand):
- Win if Redwood accepts 2-week dedicated POC + transparent kernel/quantization perf notes.
- Keep SE involved for kernel selection guidance and to size reserved GPUs precisely (Leah owns technical sizing).
- Legal to get draft SLA (with credit table) before procurement loop.
